tips.title: Sudden severe headache and sweating after spinal cord injury: first help the person sit upright, loosen tight clothing, and call 112.
tips.cost: No cost at all. Just three simple actions, completed in just a few dozen seconds.
tips.inPlainWords: In people with spinal cord injury, the body’s warning signals get disrupted. Even though the bladder may be full or clothing might be tight, the person might not notice it — yet blood pressure can spike dramatically. The warning signs are sudden severe headache and sweating. In such cases, the first step is to help the person sit upright, loosen any tight clothing, check whether the bladder is full, and call 112 right away.
tips.benefit: This episode is known as autonomic dysreflexia. A systematic review examined four major databases — Medline, CINAHL, EMBASE, and PsycINFO — and included 31 studies, 6 of which were randomized controlled trials. The review clearly states that non-drug management during an episode consists of three steps: positioning the patient upright, loosening tight clothing, and removing any triggering factors. These steps are supported by clinical consensus and physiological evidence, and are classified as Level 5 evidence. Antihypertensive drugs are only used when blood pressure remains elevated; phentolamine has Level 1 evidence, while nifedipine and prostaglandin E2 have Level 2 evidence. Preventive strategies mainly target common triggers such as urinary retention and surgical procedures; most of these preventive measures are backed by Level 4 or Level 5 evidence.
tips.sources: Krassioukov A, Warburton DE, Teasell R, Eng JJ; Spinal Cord Injury Rehabilitation Evidence Research Team (2009). A systematic review of the management of autonomic dysreflexia after spinal cord injury. Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, 90(4):682-695. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apmr.2008.10.017>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. <https://depwd.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: This B rating reflects the fact that there are no randomized controlled trials supporting those three immediate actions — only clinical consensus and physiological reasoning. The review itself notes that most of these measures are supported solely by non-controlled studies. Medication administration is strictly a medical professional’s responsibility; family members must not give antihypertensive drugs at home. Lying the person down can further raise blood pressure, so sitting upright is essential. Family members and caregivers must also master these three steps. This condition must never be mistaken for ordinary headaches.

tips.title: The first decade after becoming disabled is a high-risk period for suicide; this shouldn’t be dismissed as “just a matter of staying positive.”
tips.cost: No cost at all. It only requires a phone call or a single appointment booking.
tips.inPlainWords: In the first few years after becoming disabled, it’s very common for both the disabled individual and their family members to experience severe emotional distress — this is not a sign of weak willpower at all. Long-term follow-up studies conducted at two spinal cord injury centers in the UK found that the suicide rate among this group is five times higher than that of the general population. Over 90% of all suicides among these individuals occur within the first decade after their injury. For people whose injury was directly caused by a prior suicide attempt, this risk is even higher.
tips.benefit: This study tracked 2,304 patients with traumatic spinal cord injuries who were newly admitted between 1991 and 2010, survived the first year after injury, and had residual neurological impairments at discharge, with follow-up lasting until the end of 2014. Among them, 63 patients (2.7%) had suffered their injury as a direct result of a prior suicide attempt. By the end of the follow-up period, 533 patients had died, of which 4.2% died by suicide; 91% of all suicides occurred within the first ten years after injury. The age-standardized suicide mortality rate was 62.5 cases per 100,000 people per year (95% CI 36.4–88.6), which is five times the average suicide rate of 12.2 cases per 100,000 people in England and Wales in 2014. Compared to patients with other causes of injury, those whose injury was triggered by a prior suicide attempt had a 4.32-fold higher risk of death overall (P<0.001), and a 9.46-fold higher risk of suicide specifically (P<0.001).
tips.sources: Savic G, DeVivo MJ, Frankel HL, Jamous MA, Soni BM, Charlifue S (2018). Suicide and traumatic spinal cord injury - a cohort study. Spinal Cord, 56(1):2-6. <https://doi.org/10.1038/sc.2017.98>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. <https://depwd.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: This research was limited to spinal cord injury patients only, so the findings should be extrapolated with caution to other causes of disability such as blindness, amputation, or burns. Its main takeaway is the time window of heightened risk: this elevated risk does not fade away immediately after discharge, and requires close monitoring for a full decade. For support services, please refer to Section 29, Item 11 (14416 (Tele-MANAS)). To prevent accidental harm, avoid storing sleeping pills or pesticides at home; see Section 1, Item 25 (thoughts of suicide). If feelings of grief and emotional distress persist for more than six months, seek help from a psychiatrist or clinical psychologist; see Section 29, Item 8 (grief lasting over half a year).

tips.title: A psychiatric admission in India does not need a guardian to sign: the Mental Healthcare Act uses a nominated representative and a review board
tips.cost: Government psychiatric hospitals and district hospitals charge nothing or a token amount, and the Act gives a right to affordable care. A private psychiatric hospital charges its own daily rate, which varies widely by city and by whether the ward is general or single-occupancy.
tips.inPlainWords: If a person with a mental illness has the capacity to consent, they are admitted as a voluntary patient and can leave when they choose. If they lack that capacity, the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 allows a supported admission of up to 30 days on the application of the person's nominated representative, but only after two independent psychiatric assessments certify that admission is necessary. Nobody has to sign as a guardian, and there is no separate right to a second evaluation after three days: instead the person's capacity is reviewed every 15 days, and the Mental Health Review Board must review the admission. An advance directive and a nominated representative can be put in place in advance, while the person is well.
tips.benefit: The Act gives every person the right to free or affordable mental health care from the state, and it makes the nominated representative the person who is consulted, not a guardian who decides. Sections 4 and 5 deal with capacity and the advance directive, section 14 with the nominated representative, section 89 with a supported admission that lasts up to 30 days, section 90 with a longer admission of 30 to 90 days that needs the Board's approval, and sections 73 to 82 with the Mental Health Review Board. Section 88 covers discharge: a voluntary patient can leave, and a supported patient must be discharged when the grounds end.
tips.sources: India Code, Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 (Act 10 of 2017). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, mental health programmes. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>; National Legal Services Authority, legal aid for persons with mental illness. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: If the person lacks capacity and has not named a nominated representative, the hospital has to follow the Act's procedure for that case, and a relative cannot simply admit them as a guardian. Keep the admission papers, the two assessment reports and the Board reference number. If the person asks to leave and is not discharged, or the 15-day review does not happen, complain to the hospital's medical superintendent, then to the State Mental Health Authority and the Review Board. An emergency can justify a short admission while the paperwork is completed, but it still has to be reported and reviewed.

tips.title: For caregivers of disabled family members at home, it’s vital to watch your own health
tips.cost: There’s no cost involved. Simply share some of the caregiving duties and use that time to get a medical checkup.
tips.inPlainWords: It’s not exaggeration when caregivers feel completely exhausted. One U.S. study followed over 800 older adults for four years. Those caring for a disabled spouse while also reporting high levels of mental strain had a mortality risk roughly 63% higher than people who weren’t caregivers. No such increase appeared among caregivers who didn’t report feeling stressed. So the real issue isn’t caregiving itself, but the long-term strain it causes.
tips.benefit: This prospective cohort study ran from 1993 to 1998, with an average follow-up period of 4.5 years across four U.S. communities. It included 392 caregivers and 427 non-caregivers aged 66–96 who all lived with their spouses. Over four years, 103 participants (12.6%) passed away. After adjusting for socioeconomic factors, pre-existing conditions, and subclinical cardiovascular disease, caregivers reporting mental or emotional stress had a 63% higher mortality risk compared to non-caregivers (RR 1.63, 95% CI 1.00–2.65). No significant increase in mortality was seen among caregivers without reported stress (RR 1.08, 95% CI 0.61–1.90) or among spouses who were disabled but not cared for by their partners (RR 1.37, 95% CI 0.73–2.58).
tips.sources: Schulz R, Beach SR (1999). Caregiving as a risk factor for mortality: the Caregiver Health Effects Study. JAMA, 282(23):2215-2219. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.282.23.2215>
tips.caveats: Caution: The lower bound of the confidence interval here is exactly 1.00, meaning there remains a small chance that no actual difference exists. This study focused on older U.S. adults living with disabled spouses, so its findings may not fully apply to caregivers of younger disabled family members. Still, it clearly shows that those experiencing high stress face greater risk. Whenever possible, share caregiving duties with others; contact local disability associations and civil affairs bureaus for respite care or day programs. Caregivers should also keep taking any prescribed medications — see Section 16, Item 1. The main beneficiary of all this advice is you.

tips.title: For long‑term wheelchair users, switch to a pressure‑relieving cushion and check the ischial and sacrococcygeal areas daily
tips.cost: A pressure‑relieving cushion costs several hundred to over a thousand rupees. The daily check takes just one minute.
tips.inPlainWords: Regular foam cushions can cause skin breakdown after prolonged pressure. Once broken, the skin heals slowly and is prone to infection. In a trial conducted in nursing homes, the group using pressure‑relieving cushions showed significantly fewer pressure ulcers on the ischial region. Wheelchairs must also be sized to each individual; a generic model does not suffice.
tips.benefit: This randomized clinical trial took place in 12 nursing homes between 2004 and 2008, enrolling 232 residents aged 65 or older who used a wheelchair for at least 6 hours daily and had a Braden score ≤18. All participants received a properly fitted wheelchair and were then randomly assigned to two groups: one used skin‑protective cushions (air, viscoelastic fluid plus foam, or gel plus foam), while the other used segmented foam cushions 7.6 cm thick. Follow‑up lasted 6 months or until a pressure ulcer developed. For pressure ulcers at the ischial tuberosity, the segmented foam group had 8 cases (6.7%) versus 1 case (0.9%) in the skin‑protective group (P = 0.04). When both ischial and sacrococcygeal ulcers were counted, the segmented foam group had 21 cases (17.6%) and the skin‑protective group 12 cases (10.6%); this difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.14).
tips.sources: Brienza D, Kelsey S, Karg P, et al. (2010). A randomized clinical trial on preventing pressure ulcers with wheelchair seat cushions. Journal of the American Geriatrics Society, 58(12):2308-2314. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1532-5415.2010.03168.x>
tips.caveats: Two factors justify a B rating. First, the sample size was only 232 participants; the P‑value for the primary outcome (0.04) barely crossed the threshold, while secondary outcomes showed no difference. Second, the participants were elderly nursing‑home residents; results may not apply to younger wheelchair users. Since all subjects received a properly fitted wheelchair, both “proper fit” and “cushion type” contributed to outcomes; therefore, merely swapping the cushion is insufficient. For pressure‑ulcer prevention in bedridden individuals, air mattresses and regular repositioning are discussed in Section 17, Item 8 (Pressure ulcers). Information on applying for subsidies for basic assistive devices can be found in Section 7 of this chapter (contact the district disability office).

tips.title: Do not buy a therapy or device that claims to cure paralysis, blindness or deafness
tips.cost: No cost to ask for the evidence. A second opinion from a government hospital is cheap.
tips.inPlainWords: No therapy or device has been proven to cure a complete spinal-cord injury, a mature cataract or a sensorineural hearing loss. A claim to 'cure' paralysis, blindness or deafness is a red flag. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 give you a remedy, and the medical council can act on a false claim. Ask for the evidence, not a testimonial.
tips.benefit: The RPwD Act, 2016 protects the rights of a person with a disability and prohibits discrimination. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 covers a misleading advertisement and a deficient service. The National Medical Commission and the state medical council can act on a false claim by a doctor. A device needs a CDSCO registration where it is a medical device. A 'miracle cure' that delays a proven treatment can cause harm.
tips.sources: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; National Medical Commission. <https://www.nmc.org.in/>; Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation. <https://cdsco.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Rehabilitation, physiotherapy and assistive devices can improve function; they are not a cure. A claim based only on testimonials is not evidence. Do not stop a proven treatment for a miracle cure.

tips.title: The one card that unlocks most Indian disability benefits is the UDID; the pension itself is paid by your state
tips.cost: The UDID application itself is free on the portal, though a state may charge a small fee for the assessment or the printed card. Applying for the pension is free. Anyone offering to get you a UDID quickly for a fee is selling you something the portal does for nothing.
tips.inPlainWords: The Unique Disability ID card, or UDID, is the certificate most Indian disability schemes ask for. You apply on swavlambancard.gov.in, choose a government hospital, and a medical board assesses your disability; the card is then issued with a percentage and a disability code. With it you can apply for the state disability pension or allowance, the ADIP scheme for devices, Niramaya insurance, the income-tax deductions under sections 80U and 80DD, the 4 per cent reservation in government posts, and free or concessional travel where your state offers it. No single office hands all of this over at once: the card is central, but the pension amount and the extra benefits are set by each state, so the district social welfare office or the state disability directorate is where you apply for those.
tips.benefit: The portal lets you track the application, download a soft copy and correct an error. A benchmark disability of 40 per cent or more is what most schemes require, and a higher percentage unlocks more: for example the ADIP income-linked subsidy and the higher income-tax deduction depend on it. The state pension is usually claimed with the UDID, a bank account in the applicant's name, an income or residence certificate and a photograph, and many states pay a higher rate at 80 per cent or more. Because the card is a single national record, it also makes it easier to carry one document instead of a district certificate plus a hospital letter.
tips.sources: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Unique Disability ID. <https://swavlambancard.gov.in/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, UDID. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/unique-disability-id-udid/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, schemes and services. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/schemes-and-services/>
tips.caveats: The disability percentage on the card is what the medical board assessed, and it can be reviewed if the condition changes. A pension from one state usually stops when you move to another, because the scheme is state-funded, so tell the new district office before you move. The UDID does not replace every document: a railway concession and some scholarships ask for their own form or a specific certificate. Keep a scanned copy and note the UDID number, because you will need it repeatedly.

tips.title: For a child under six the Indian help is devices, insurance and early intervention, not a national therapy allowance
tips.cost: ADIP is free or half price according to the income slab, and the device has to be bought through an implementing agency or the PMD-VK and ARJUN portals. Niramaya charges a small annual premium set by the National Trust, so check the current rate on its site rather than relying on an old figure. Government hospital therapy is charged at the hospital's own nominal rates.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no national cash benefit that pays for a young child's therapy. What does exist is a set of separate schemes. The ADIP scheme pays most of the cost of aids and appliances for a family below an income ceiling. Niramaya, run by the National Trust, is a low-cost insurance policy for autism, cerebral palsy, intellectual disability and multiple disabilities that reimburses therapy, hospitalisation and corrective surgery up to a fixed yearly limit. The DDRS scheme funds non-governmental organisations that run early intervention and day-care services, the cross-disability early intervention centres assess and start therapy, and a government hospital's physical medicine and rehabilitation department is the cheapest place to begin. Apply with the UDID.
tips.benefit: ADIP pays 100 per cent of the cost of an aid if the family's monthly income is Rs 22,500 or less, and 50 per cent if it is between Rs 22,501 and Rs 30,000, up to Rs 15,000 for most aids once in three years, up to Rs 30,000 for a high-end prosthesis, and up to Rs 50,000 towards a motorised tricycle or wheelchair once in five years. Niramaya gives cover of Rs 1 lakh on a reimbursement basis, with no pre-insurance medical test, at any hospital, for a person holding a UDID with one of the four National Trust disabilities. The DDRS grant reaches you through an NGO, so ask the district office which nearby organisation holds one.
tips.sources: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, ADIP scheme. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/adip-scheme/>; National Trust, Niramaya health insurance. <https://nationaltrust.nic.in/about-niramaya/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, DDRS. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/ddrs/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, cross-disability early intervention centres. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/cross-disability-early-intervention-centres/>
tips.caveats: ADIP covers a given device once in three years, or once in five years for a motorised wheelchair, so plan the purchase and keep the receipt. Niramaya pays after you spend, so keep every prescription, bill and discharge summary, and remember that it is not a substitute for a health insurance policy. The income ceiling is the family's, and a household just above it pays the full market price. Private therapy is not covered by any national scheme, and the quality and cost of therapists vary widely.

tips.title: No national subsidy pays to adapt a private home; some states and municipal bodies do, and the rest is your own cost
tips.cost: Where a state grant exists it is small and capped, and it may be paid only after the work is finished and inspected. Otherwise the whole cost is yours, and a contractor's quotation is the only reliable figure.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no central scheme that pays to widen a doorway, build a ramp or convert a bathroom in a private house. The accessibility duties in the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 fall on public buildings, transport, information and services, not on your landlord and not on your own home. What you can use: some states and municipal corporations run small grants or distribute ramps, grab rails and commode chairs through the district disability office; the ADIP scheme funds devices rather than construction; and a request to a landlord for a ramp is a reasonable request, though the Act does not force a private landlord to pay for it.
tips.benefit: The practical route is a written application to the district social welfare officer or the state disability directorate asking whether a home-modification or independent-living grant exists in your state, with the UDID, income proof, a photograph of the entrance and a quotation from a contractor. Some municipal corporations attach a disability cell to their building-permission department, which can advise on a ramp that does not need approval. Where no grant exists, the cheapest changes are usually a portable ramp, a raised toilet seat and grab rails, and those are the items ADIP is most likely to fund.
tips.sources: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, schemes and services. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/schemes-and-services/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, ADIP scheme. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/adip-scheme/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, the RPwD Act, 2016 and its rules. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/rpwd-act-2016/>
tips.caveats: Do not pay anyone who promises a central home-modification subsidy: there is no such scheme. A landlord's refusal to build a ramp is not automatically unlawful, because the Act's accessibility duties do not bind a private dwelling. Put a request to a landlord in writing, keep the reply, and consider a portable ramp that you can take with you. If you rent a flat in a building with a residents' association, the association's approval is a separate step from the landlord's.

tips.title: Mention your disability certificate in a job application: it can bring a reservation, a concession or a support
tips.cost: The certificate is free or low cost. A private employer's support varies.
tips.inPlainWords: A disability certificate and a UDID can make you eligible for a reservation in a government post, a fee concession, a scholarship and a workplace accommodation. Mention it at the application stage, not only at the interview, and keep a copy of the certificate. A private employer may also get a benefit for employing a person with a disability. You do not have to disclose a disability that does not affect the job, but a support or a reservation usually needs the certificate.
tips.benefit: The RPwD Act, 2016 provides a 4% reservation in government establishments for the identified disabilities and requires an equal-opportunity policy. The UDID card is the single document for the benefits. A private employer can claim a deduction under the Income-tax Act for employing a person with a disability. The Act prohibits discrimination in promotion and pay. A reasonable accommodation can include a ramp, a screen reader or flexible hours.
tips.sources: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. <https://depwd.gov.in/>; Income-tax Department. <https://www.incometax.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A reservation applies to an identified post and a government establishment. A private employer is not bound by the 4% quota, but is bound by the anti-discrimination provisions. Keep the medical records for a reassessment.

tips.title: The income-tax deduction for your own disability is section 80U; for a dependant it is section 80DD
tips.cost: The certificate is issued by a government hospital's medical board and is free or charged at the hospital's nominal rate. A tax preparer's fee is optional, and the portal walks you through the claim.
tips.inPlainWords: If you have a disability of 40 per cent or more, section 80U lets you deduct Rs 75,000 from your taxable income, and if the disability is 80 per cent or more the deduction is Rs 1,25,000. If you support a dependant with a disability, section 80DD gives the same two amounts, and the money does not have to be spent on treatment: it can go towards their care, nursing or a trained attendant. You claim it in your income-tax return with a certificate from a government medical authority. There is no office to visit and no application to a tax officer, and no agent needs to be paid to get it.
tips.benefit: The deduction is a flat amount, so it does not depend on how much you actually spent, and it is available every year that the disability continues. Section 80U is claimed by the person with the disability; section 80DD is claimed by the relative who supports them, and the dependant must be wholly dependent on that person. Only one of the two can be used for the same person in a year, so a family where the person with a disability has their own taxable income should decide which claim saves more. A severe disability at 80 per cent or more gives the higher figure under both sections.
tips.sources: Income Tax Department, e-filing portal. <https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/>; Income Tax Department, deductions for disability. <https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, UDID. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/unique-disability-id-udid/>
tips.caveats: This is a deduction, not a payment: it reduces taxable income, so the saving is your marginal tax rate multiplied by the amount. If you file under the new regime in section 115BAC, most deductions of this kind are withdrawn, so work out both regimes before choosing, because for a family with a large medical bill the old regime can still be better. A certificate must be renewed if the disability changes, and a false certificate is an offence. Keep the certificate and the acknowledgement with your return papers.

tips.title: Buses have to be accessible under the RPwD Act, but free travel is a state concession, not a national right
tips.cost: Free where your city or state funds the concession; otherwise the ordinary fare, or a discounted pass at the rate the undertaking sets. The pass itself is usually free or nominal.
tips.inPlainWords: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 requires public transport to be made accessible, and it obliges the government to provide transport for a child with a disability and an attendant to reach school. What it does not do is make bus travel free everywhere. Free or concessional travel is decided by each state and each city transport undertaking: some cities have long allowed free travel for people with disabilities on their buses, others give a concession, and some give nothing. Ask the transport undertaking in your city what it offers and which document it wants, and ask the state disability department whether a bus pass scheme exists.
tips.benefit: Sections 40 to 46 of the Act deal with accessibility of the built environment, transport, information and communication, and consumer goods, and the Accessible India Campaign audits and retrofits public transport and railway stations. Where a pass exists it is usually issued against the UDID or a disability certificate at a depot or online, and it may cover a companion as well. If a conductor refuses a valid concession, or a driver passes a wheelchair user by, that is a complaint to the transport undertaking and to the state commissioner for persons with disabilities, not something you have to argue on the footboard.
tips.sources: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, the RPwD Act, 2016 and its rules. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/rpwd-act-2016/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, schemes and services. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/schemes-and-services/>; Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. <https://morth.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: There is no statutory right to free travel across India, so a refusal in a city without a scheme is not necessarily unlawful. Assistance dogs are a gap: Indian law does not give a trained service dog a general right of entry the way some countries do, so ask the operator in advance and expect to negotiate. Accessible buses are unevenly rolled out, and a low-floor bus is not the same as an accessible stop. For a complaint, keep the bus number, the time and the route.

tips.title: Exam boards must give accommodation, but you have to ask with your certificate before the form closes
tips.cost: The accommodation itself is free. A board or agency usually arranges the scribe, and where you bring your own, its eligibility rules apply.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian exam bodies publish a list of facilities for candidates with disabilities: a scribe, extra time, a separate room, a magnifier, an assistive device, and in some exams a choice of centre. You get them by declaring the disability and uploading the certificate when you apply, not by asking the invigilator on the day. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act requires educational institutions to provide the support, and the Central Board of Secondary Education, the National Testing Agency for CUET and NEET, and each state board publish their own rules and deadlines in the examination bulletin. Read the bulletin for your exam before the form closes.
tips.benefit: The usual steps are: tick the disability option in the application, upload the UDID or the disability certificate, apply separately for a scribe where the exam allows one, and carry the admit card, the certificate and an identity document to the centre. If the centre cannot provide what was approved, ask for the centre superintendent and put the request in writing on the spot, then complain to the board or the testing agency afterwards with the acknowledgement. The state commissioner for persons with disabilities can take up a persistent refusal.
tips.sources: Central Board of Secondary Education, academic and examination circulars. <https://cbseacademic.nic.in/>; National Testing Agency. <https://nta.ac.in/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, the RPwD Act, 2016 and its rules. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/rpwd-act-2016/>
tips.caveats: Deadlines are strict and a request made after the correction window is normally refused, so diarise the date. The percentage of extra time and the list of permitted devices differ from exam to exam and change between years, so read the current bulletin rather than a senior's account. A scribe is usually required to be a student of a lower standard and not a relative. If a centre is physically inaccessible, ask for a change of centre when you apply, because it cannot be fixed on the day.

tips.title: School is a right under the RTE Act and the RPwD Act; home-based education is the fallback, not the first choice
tips.cost: A government school is free, including textbooks, uniform and the mid-day meal. A private school's fee is its own, but a seat under the RTE quota costs the parent nothing.
tips.inPlainWords: The Right to Education Act gives every child aged six to fourteen free and compulsory education in a neighbourhood school, and the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act adds that a school must admit a child with a disability without discrimination and provide the support the child needs. Where a child cannot attend even with that support, the law treats home-based education as an alternative that the state education department has to arrange, not something a parent has to organise alone. A school that refuses admission, charges a capitation fee, or pushes a child out because of the disability is breaking the law, and the remedy starts with a written complaint to the district education officer.
tips.benefit: Section 16 of the RPwD Act lists the duties of an educational institution, including admitting a child without discrimination, providing the facilities the child needs, and arranging transport for the child and an attendant; section 17 sets out the measures for inclusive education. Under the RTE Act the neighbourhood school cannot charge a fee, and the 25 per cent entry-level quota in private schools is free to the parent. The Samagra Shiksha programme funds resource teachers, aids and ramps in government schools, so ask the block education officer what the school can claim.
tips.sources: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, the RPwD Act, 2016 and its rules. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/rpwd-act-2016/>; Ministry of Education. <https://www.education.gov.in/>; Central Board of Secondary Education, academic circulars. <https://cbseacademic.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Home-based education is meant for a child who cannot attend even with support, and the state has to arrange it; a school cannot use it to avoid admitting the child. Put a refusal in writing with the date and the name of the person who refused, because a complaint without a record is easy to deny. The RTE Act covers ages six to fourteen, so for an older child the RPwD Act and the state's scheme apply, and for a younger child the anganwadi and early intervention route. Expelling a child because of a disability is discrimination, not discipline.

tips.title: India has no separate disability licence: you take the ordinary test at the RTO, with a medical certificate and an adapted car
tips.cost: The RTO fee is set by the state and is listed on the Parivahan portal; a driving school and an adaptation workshop charge separately, and the adaptation is the large item.
tips.inPlainWords: Unlike some countries, India does not issue a special category of driving licence for people with disabilities. You apply for an ordinary learner's licence and then a permanent licence at the regional transport office, and the medical certificate the RTO requires has to state that you are fit to drive, with any adaptation noted. A car fitted with hand controls, a left-foot accelerator or an automatic gearbox can be driven once the adaptation is recorded, and some offices ask you to take the test in that car. For a hearing impairment the office may ask for a specialist's opinion; for uncontrolled epilepsy or poor vision the fitness rules are stricter.
tips.benefit: The application is made on the Parivahan portal or at the RTO, with Form 1 for the medical certificate and Form 1A where the office asks for it, photographs and address proof, and the learner's test is a short computer or oral test on road rules. A licence issued with an adaptation carries that condition, which is what an insurer and a traffic officer look for. The vehicle itself must be adapted by a workshop that will give you a written certificate of the work, and the insurance policy should record the adaptation so that a claim is not refused on the ground that the car was modified.
tips.sources: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Parivahan Sewa. <https://parivahan.gov.in/parivahan/>; Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. <https://morth.gov.in/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, the RPwD Act, 2016 and its rules. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/rpwd-act-2016/>
tips.caveats: Practice varies between states and even between offices, so telephone the RTO before you go and ask which form it wants for your disability. A refusal has to be in writing, and it can be challenged before the transport commissioner. A licence is not a right to drive unsafely: if the condition changes, or a seizure happens, you have to stop and be reassessed. Do not let a driving school promise a licence without the medical step; that is how licences get cancelled later.

tips.title: Rehabilitation should be carried out at a proper facility with a rehabilitation medicine department; the intensity must be set by therapists — more intensity does not necessarily mean better results.
tips.cost: Inpatient rehabilitation costs a few hundred rupees per day; the out‑of‑pocket portion varies by region. Treatment is billed on a monthly basis. Daily exercises are required and can be quite monotonous.
tips.inPlainWords: The most common mistake is simply sending a patient home to lie down and hope for a natural recovery. Care delivered by a coordinated, multidisciplinary team helps many patients survive one year later and continue living at home. However, patients should not overdo it on their own. In a large multi-center clinical trial, early, frequent, and more intensive activity within 24 hours after a stroke actually led to poorer outcomes three months later. Thus, the amount and timing of exercise must be determined by the rehabilitation department and therapists.
tips.benefit: A Cochrane systematic review included 29 trials with 5,902 participants, comparing organized inpatient stroke‑unit care with other forms of care. At the final follow‑up (median 1 year), the odds ratio for adverse outcomes — death, disability, or need for institutional care — was 0.77 (95% CI 0.69–0.87). The odds ratio for death alone was 0.76 (95% CI 0.66–0.88), and for death or dependence it was 0.75 (95% CI 0.66–0.85); evidence quality is moderate. In absolute terms, for every 100 patients receiving stroke‑unit care, an additional 2 survive, 6 continue living at home, and 6 regain the ability to care for themselves. Conversely, the AVERT trial randomly assigned 2,104 patients across 56 acute stroke units in five countries to either “standard care” or “standard care plus very early intensive activity.” After three months, 480 patients (46%) in the early‑activity group achieved a good outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0–2) versus 525 patients (50%) in the standard‑care group; the adjusted odds ratio was 0.73 (95% CI 0.59–0.90, P=0.004). Death rates were 88 versus 72 patients, with no statistically significant difference (odds ratio 1.34, 95% CI 0.93–1.93, P=0.113).
tips.sources: Langhorne P, Ramachandra S; Stroke Unit Trialists' Collaboration (2020). Organised inpatient (stroke unit) care for stroke: network meta-analysis. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 4:CD000197. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000197.pub4>; AVERT Trial Collaboration group (2015). Efficacy and safety of very early mobilisation within 24 h of stroke onset (AVERT): a randomised controlled trial. Lancet, 386(9988):46-55. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)60690-0>
tips.caveats: Caution: Both studies involve stroke patients; their findings cannot be directly applied to other disabling conditions such as spinal cord injury, amputation, or burns. The AVERT trial demonstrates that “the earlier and more intense the activity, the better” is not true; it does not mean that early activity is useless. In both trials, the majority of participants began walking within 24 hours; the difference lay in frequency and total volume of exercise. When selecting a facility, verify whether it has a rehabilitation medicine department and qualified physical and occupational therapists — do not rely solely on a “rehabilitation” sign. Information on referrals between primary and tertiary hospitals and related cost thresholds can be found in Section 24.1 (step‑by‑step referrals). Community‑based rehabilitation and assistive devices are discussed in Section 16.7 (contact the district disability office).

tips.title: Getting a hearing aid when hearing declines — the reason is to hear better now, not to prevent dementia
tips.cost: Hearing aids cost several thousand to tens of thousands of rupees; most must be paid for out of pocket. Fitting requires professional testing and multiple follow‑up adjustments.
tips.inPlainWords: The claim that “wearing a hearing aid prevents dementia” currently lacks solid evidence. A three‑year trial involving nearly a thousand participants found no overall difference between groups. Only among people already at higher risk of cognitive decline did a modest benefit appear. Thus, the main reason to get a hearing aid is to hear clearly now — to talk with others and hear traffic while crossing the street — not to protect the brain decades later.
tips.benefit: The ACHIEVE trial took place in four U.S. communities and enrolled 977 individuals aged 70–84 with untreated hearing loss but no obvious cognitive impairment. Participants were randomly assigned to either hearing intervention (counseling and hearing aid fitting) or health‑education control, with follow‑up every six months. The primary endpoint was change in overall cognitive scores over three years. In the combined analysis of both participant cohorts, there was no significant difference: the intervention group showed a change of −0.200 (95% CI −0.256 to −0.144) versus −0.202 (95% CI −0.258 to −0.145) in the control group; the difference was 0.002 (95% CI −0.077 to 0.081, P = 0.96). A pre‑specified sensitivity analysis revealed a statistically significant interaction (P = 0.010) between the two cohorts. The second cohort comprised older participants with more risk factors for cognitive decline and lower baseline cognitive scores. Researchers concluded that hearing intervention may modestly slow cognitive decline over three years in high‑risk individuals but not in those at lower risk. No serious adverse events attributable to the intervention were reported.
tips.sources: Lin FR, Pike JR, Albert MS, et al.; ACHIEVE Collaborative Research Group (2023). Hearing intervention versus health education control to reduce cognitive decline in older adults with hearing loss in the USA (ACHIEVE): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial. Lancet, 402(10404):786-797. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(23)01406-X>
tips.caveats: Controversy: The oft‑quoted claim that “hearing aids cut cognitive decline by nearly half” stems from a subgroup analysis of this trial, not its primary result, which showed no overall difference. This note is included to separate the practical benefit of hearing aids from the unproven dementia‑prevention claim. Students with hearing impairments may be exempt from foreign‑language listening tests in college entrance exams; see item 13 (reasonable accommodations) in this section. Drivers with hearing loss should wear hearing aids; see item 15 (C5) in this section.

tips.title: No court now declares an adult with a disability wholly incapable; Indian law uses support and limited guardianship
tips.cost: A court application costs court fees and a lawyer's fee, and it takes months. The National Trust committee route is cheaper and faster but is limited to its four disabilities.
tips.inPlainWords: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 states that a person with a disability enjoys legal capacity on an equal basis with others, and it replaced the old model in which a court declared someone of unsound mind incapable and appointed a guardian over everything. Now a district court, or an authority the state government notifies, can appoint only a limited guardian: a joint arrangement for a specific decision and a specific period, made according to the person's own will, and only where the person has been given support and still cannot take a legally binding decision. Total support is exceptional and is reviewed. Every guardian appointed before the Act is treated as a limited guardian.
tips.benefit: In practice the person keeps the right to decide about their money, property, treatment, marriage and vote, and a guardian's signature is not needed for ordinary decisions. Where a bank, a registrar or a hospital insists on a guardian, quote sections 13 and 14 and ask for the refusal in writing, then take it to the state commissioner for persons with disabilities. For the four disabilities covered by the National Trust Act, a local level committee can appoint a guardian under section 14 of that Act, which is a separate and usually quicker route for autism, cerebral palsy, intellectual disability and multiple disabilities.
tips.sources: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, the RPwD Act, 2016 and its rules. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/rpwd-act-2016/>; National Trust, legal guardianship. <https://nationaltrust.nic.in/about-legal-guardianship/>; India Code. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: The Act does not abolish guardianship for children: a minor's property is still dealt with under the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890. A limited guardianship order can be reviewed and appealed, and it does not transfer the person's rights to the guardian. If a relative is managing someone's money without any order, that is a civil dispute about the money, not a legal guardianship, and it should be challenged rather than regularised. Keep the order, the period and the decisions it covers in writing.

tips.title: A guardian in India is not automatically liable for harm an adult with a disability causes; that adult's own assets are answerable
tips.cost: Insurance premiums depend on the cover; legal aid through the district legal services authority is free for a person who qualifies, and NALSA's network can advise before a claim is filed.
tips.inPlainWords: There is no Indian rule that makes a guardian pay for damage an adult with a disability causes, the way a parent answers for a young child. An adult is responsible for their own civil wrongs, and a court can order compensation out of that person's assets; a limited guardian appointed under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act decides jointly with the person on specified matters and does not become an insurer of their conduct. For a minor, the parents are liable. What actually protects a family is insurance and paperwork, not a guardian's promise: a personal accident policy, a householder's liability cover, and for a driver a motor policy that records any adaptation.
tips.benefit: A limited guardian should keep the person's money separate, record what was spent and why, and keep the appointment order with the list of decisions it covers, because that record is what a court will look at if a dispute arises. If a claim is threatened, the person's own insurer conducts the defence and the guardian is not a party unless the guardian did something wrong. A guardian who takes money or neglects the person is personally liable for that, and can be removed by the court or authority that appointed them.
tips.sources: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, the RPwD Act, 2016 and its rules. <https://depwd.gov.in/en/rpwd-act-2016/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>; India Code. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: This is a general account, not advice on a specific case: the facts decide, and a lawyer should see the papers. Do not sign an undertaking that you are responsible for all harm the person may cause, because no law requires it and a signed undertaking can be enforced as a contract. Guardianship is not a way to take over someone's property, and a transfer made by a limited guardian outside the order can be set aside. If a relative is already acting as a guardian without an order, regularise it or stop.

tips.title: If you are denied a job, a promotion or equal pay because of a disability, the RPwD Act gives you a remedy
tips.cost: No cost to complain to the commissioner. A lawyer's fee for a court case; legal aid is available.
tips.inPlainWords: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 prohibits discrimination in employment, promotion and pay, and requires a reasonable accommodation. A government establishment must follow the reservation and the equal-opportunity policy. A private employer must not discriminate. You can complain to the state commissioner for persons with disabilities, the labour authority or a court. Keep the advertisement, the emails and the pay records.
tips.benefit: Sections 20 and 21 of the RPwD Act, 2016 prohibit discrimination and require an equal-opportunity policy. The state commissioner can inquire into a complaint and recommend action. The labour court or the civil court can award compensation. The Act also provides for a grievance redressal officer in a government establishment. A union or an NGO can help with the complaint.
tips.sources: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. <https://depwd.gov.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A 'disability' must fall within the Act's list and be certified. A delay can weaken the case. A settlement should be in writing.

tips.title: For neurogenic bladder retention following spinal cord injury, decide bladder management jointly with your urologist, avoid unattended permanent indwelling catheters, and maintain lifelong surveillance of kidneys and bladder
tips.cost: Performing clean intermittent self-catheterization (CIC) 4 to 6 times daily requires continuing supply expenditures for catheters and a few minutes per session. Follow-up clinic visits every 1 to 2 years at urology or physical medicine and rehabilitation clinics. The friction is maintaining rigid daily catheterization discipline without interruption for decades.
tips.inPlainWords: Following spinal cord injury, the bladder frequently loses reflexive voiding, requiring artificial drainage to prevent renal damage. A 70-year longitudinal British cohort showed that over 11% of late deaths in spinal cord injury patients stemmed from genitourinary complications. Individuals with long-term indwelling transurethral catheters suffer roughly twice the rate of urological complications compared to clean intermittent self-catheterization. Regardless of chosen technique, patients must maintain lifelong regular urological monitoring.
tips.benefit: A landmark 70-year British follow-up study across two spinal cord injury centers evaluated 5,483 traumatic spinal cord injury patients injured between 1943 and 2010 who survived beyond the first post-injury year. Among 2,170 decedents with reliable cause-of-death determinations, genitourinary diseases accounted for 11.5% of all late deaths (following respiratory causes at 29.3%, cardiovascular at 26.7%, and neoplasms at 13.9%). Age-adjusted genitourinary mortality among spinal cord injury survivors remained significantly elevated compared to the general population. In a U.S. retrospective cohort of 316 traumatic spinal cord injury patients followed for a mean of 18.3 years, the overall urological complication rate was 53.5% for indwelling transurethral catheterization, compared to 27.2% for clean intermittent catheterization (CIC), 32.4% for spontaneous voiding, and 44.4% for suprapubic cystostomy. Complications included recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs), calculi, urethral trauma, and upper tract hydronephrosis. The European Association of Urology (EAU) 2026 Guidelines on Neuro-Urology strongly discourage long-term indwelling transurethral catheterization due to elevated UTI and urethral complication rates. The EAU guidelines emphasize that lifelong regular urological follow-up is mandatory to detect silent upper urinary tract deterioration and secondary renal failure. High-risk patients require renal ultrasound every 6 months and comprehensive annual clinical evaluations and urinalysis.
tips.sources: Savic G, DeVivo MJ, Frankel HL, Jamous MA, Soni BM, Charlifue S (2017). Causes of death after traumatic spinal cord injury—a 70-year British study. Spinal Cord, 55(10):891-897. <https://doi.org/10.1038/sc.2017.64>; Weld KJ, Dmochowski RR (2000). Effect of bladder management on urological complications in spinal cord injured patients. Journal of Urology, 163(3):768-772. <https://doi.org/10.1016/s0022-5347(05)67800-7>; European Association of Urology (2026). EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (Sections 3.3.8, 3.4.2.e, 3.5.1, 3.7). <https://uroweb.org/guidelines/neuro-urology/chapter/the-guideline>
tips.caveats: Controversy: The EAU guidelines classify both intermittent catheterization and indwelling catheterization as standard clinical options, emphasizing that treatment modality should be decided through shared decision-making between patient and clinician. Among patients with tetraplegia or severe upper-limb impairment who lack reliable caregiver assistance, indwelling suprapubic or urethral catheterization may be a necessary pragmatic choice; in such cases, silicone catheters are preferred over latex to reduce encrustation and allergic reactions. Never leave an indwelling catheter unmonitored for years. Seek prompt medical care upon developing signs of urinary tract infection: fever, new or worsening urinary leakage, aggravated spasticity, malaise, cloudy or foul-smelling urine, flank pain, or autonomic dysreflexia. An overdistended bladder can precipitate life-threatening autonomic dysreflexia (see Chapter 33, Rule 1).
